thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming endpoint /v1/stream - sudden p99 spike (x10) observed, increased tail latency and partial client reconnects. Auto-page oncall. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/streaming?panel=tail_latency
Amelia: saw the page, jumping on. p95 looks OK, p99 ~ 1.8s -> 13s on a subset of requests. :eyes:
Raj: I can see elevated write latencies on the proxy layer for the EU cluster. `proxy_write_delay_ms` histogram shifted. Any deploys?
Amelia: no deploys in the last hour. No config pushes.
Kai: runtime reports increased write syscall blocking from gRPC/proxy to backend. Could be TCP slow consumers or HTTP/2 flow control.
Lucy: customers are reporting partial streams with long pauses then catch-up chunks. One ticket from AcmeInc shows their consumer saw ~7s pauses. Ticket: https://support/redwood/tickets/1345
Marta: product notified customer success to give ETA. Holding statement drafted.
Amelia: quick diagnostic checklist: 1) isolate affected routes 2) check proxy queue/backpressure 3) confirm client-side backpressure patterns 4) try short mitigation (force flushes / bump timeouts)
Raj: isolating by route now: it's concentrated on `/v1/stream` websocket and SSE paths behind the edge-proxy group eu-west-2a. Not all hosts impacted.
Kai: dumping a slow request trace:
```
[2026-03-15T13:21:08Z] request_id=abc123 stream write start
[2026-03-15T13:21:08Z] backend chunk ready -> backend write queued
[2026-03-15T13:21:09Z] proxy write blocked (EAGAIN) for 6200ms
[2026-03-15T13:21:15Z] client ACK window update delayed
[2026-03-15T13:21:21Z] proxy resumed write -> several chunks sent
```
Raj: pattern: backend producing chunks promptly; proxy can't flush to client due to slow TCP ACKs / small window, leads to head-of-line delays for other streams on same connection.
Amelia: do we expose per-connection queue length?
Kai: yes; host hst-07 has a few connections with queue depth > 50 and `last_write_ms` > 5k.
Lucy: is this client-specific (some customers) or general? Support shows ~12 distinct customer origins, not a single IP. Suggests either ISP/consumer-side pacing or a proxy-level write buffer starvation.
Amelia: mitigation options - immediate: 1) enable per-connection max-in-flight=1 (de-linearize multiplexing) 2) increase edge keepalive and write timeout to avoid connection reset 3) temporarily move heavy streaming traffic to a standby pool without HTTP/2 multiplexing. Which is least risky?
Raj: we can toggle `http2.max_concurrent_streams` down to 32 on affected hosts to reduce head-of-line. That should lower contention. Rolling config change via infra and revert after.
Kai: also a runtime patch to include chunk-level flushes: set `stream_flush_threshold_ms=50` so backend forces flush sooner. Might reduce buffering at proxy.
Amelia: do we have a fast path to reroute clients? Canary to standby pool now?
Raj: executing a canary route change for a small subset (10%) to standby pool with dedicated single-stream sockets. Command: `curl -X POST https://infra/api/route-shift -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","target":"standby-eu","percent":10}'`
Amelia: doing that. Will monitor p99 on canary.
incident-bot: ROUTE SHIFT: /v1/stream -> standby-eu (10%) started by raj.platform at 2026-03-15T13:24:10Z
Kai: after enabling `max_concurrent_streams=32` on the three hosts, observed per-host p99 drop from 12s -> 3.2s within 2 min. Good sign.
Lucy: canary traffic to standby shows p99 ~ 1.1s. Users on canary are improved.
Marta: CS updated AcmeInc with interim workaround and noted we are investigating.
Amelia: next steps: keep `max_concurrent_streams=32` in place for now, continue rolling to all affected in batch. Meanwhile plan for a longer-term fix: smarter per-connection scheduling or HTTP/2 prioritization tuning.
Raj: rolling to remaining hosts now (batch size 3). Rolling command: `./infra/roll-config --group eu-west-2a --param http2.max_concurrent_streams=32 --batch 3`
Kai: opening a follow-up ticket to add connection-level metrics: per-conn queue depth, per-stream pause counts, and histograms on `write_resume_ms`.
Amelia: logging the incident for SLO review: cause = client/connection slow-ACK + HTTP/2 multiplexing head-of-line -> increased tail latency. Severity: Sev2. Affected customers ~250 streams with p99 breaches, some reconnections.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity set to Sev2 by oncall Amelia at 2026-03-15T13:31:05Z
Lucy: any customer-facing RFO text? Draft: "We observed intermittent streaming interruptions due to intermediate proxy write congestion when clients had slow receive windows. Temporary mitigation applied (reduced multiplexing). We're working on scheduling fixes and telemetry improvements."
Marta: approved. Sending to AcmeInc and impacted list now.
Amelia: final ops note: keep `max_concurrent_streams=32` for 2 hours, monitor p99/p95, then stepwise consider `stream_flush_threshold_ms=50` rollout. Rollback plan: revert `max_concurrent_streams` and shift traffic back if errors increase.
Raj: metrics after 10m: global p99 down from 11.8s -> 2.9s, error rate unchanged.
Kai: follow-up engineering ticket: ENG-STREAM-402 - implement per-connection fair-queueing and add connection metrics.
Lucy: closing the live triage call in 10m if stable.
Amelia: good work. Please add any leftover notes here and handoff to postmortem channel when we create the doc. :thumbsup:
